ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant screening of every UBO, general partner, authorized signatory, and contributor against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list and UN Act resolutions; (ii) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) the Canadian government's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada); (iv) OFAC SDN list and sectoral sanctions as a defensive benchmark for USD clearance; (v) domestic and provincial politically exposed persons (PEP) data aggregators for foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, heads of international organizations, and family members; and (vi) adverse-media and enforcement-action database checks. Records of screening must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship; a written AML/CFT policy, a designated compliance officer, and a FINTRAC compliance regime must be in place before the first financial transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online declaration and name reservation system: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (Services en ligne / Online services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A name of a Quebec société en commandite (limited partnership) must be in French, or must have a French version; a name in another language is allowed only where accompanied by a French version and the foreign name is used in a complementary manner. Latin-script transliteration of Chinese or other non-Latin script UBO names must follow official government romanization standards and be certified by a member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec. The legal ending must be 'société en commandite', 's.e.c.', 'limited partnership', or 'L.P.', and the name must be distinct from all names already appearing in the REQ enterprise name index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any token implying royal, governmental, or military sponsorship
Any obscene, scandalous, or criminally suggestive token
Any token that misleadingly suggests public authority or an unrecognized professional title
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation rejected by the REQ may be refiled with additional justifying documentation (trademark registrations, waivers/consent letters from prior holders, or dictionary/descriptiveness submissions). If refused a second time, the applicant may submit a written administrative review request to the Registraire within 30 days of refusal, invoking section 29 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A further refusal may be appealed to the Court of Quebec (Civil Division) by way of judicial review under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, arts. 529 et seq., within 30 days of the final administrative decision. No fee is charged for a re-examination by the Registraire, but court filing fees apply upon judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A pure mail-forwarding virtual office is not acceptable; the registered office must be a real physical location in Quebec where statutory books and records are accessible and where the general partner or its mandated representative can receive service of process. Commercial executive-suite addresses with a dedicated physical office, lockable file storage, French-speaking reception personnel, and a formal agreement for documents and service of process may satisfy REQ and financial institution requirements. The RACJ alcohol wholesale permit requires a substantive commercial establishment with storage premises or a documented third-party bonded warehouse arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High quantified risk: for a new craft-brewery wholesale distributor, the Regie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) and municipal public security authorities perform a pre-license or first-year unannounced physical inspection in approximately 60% to 75% of cases; the Registraire des entreprises may also conduct a verification visit when a virtual/executive office is declared. Probabilistic risk of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation is assessed at 65%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), Articles 2161 to 2193 governing formation and operation of limited partnerships
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Formation of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; partners determine and contribute capital as specified in the partnership agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the formation of the limited partnership is hereby approved, with the general partner appointed as the general partner responsible for management and the limited partner as the limited partner; capital contributions are subscribed as per the partnership agreement; the registered office is adopted at the principal place of business in Quebec; the general partner is authorized to execute all filings and agreements; this resolution ratifies the partnership agreement and authorizes submission of the Declaration of Formation to the Registre des entreprises du Québec. The limited partnership is formed for the purpose of craft beer microbrewery distribution and wholesale operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide missing documents or clarifications within 10 business days to avoid rejection

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), GST/HST and federal Business Number programme, Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Quebec, QST administration, Registraire des entreprises du Quebec and clients portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the Quebec limited partnership agreement and file a declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; Step 2: Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) with GST/HST and Import-Export (RM) programme accounts via CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1 (immediate electronic issuance available; paper filings take 3 to 6 weeks); Step 3: If taxable supplies in Quebec exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold, register for QST with Revenu Quebec using Form LM-1-V or the online registration service and obtain the NEQ and QST account; Step 4: Register the partnership itself, not the individual partners, as the GST/HST/QST registrant; each non-resident limited partner must provide prescribed information and, if no Canadian address, appoint a representative for service of documents via CRA Form RC59; Step 5: File the annual partnership information return (T5013) and ensure GST/HST and QST returns are filed by the partnership even where no tax is payable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - flow-through taxpayer for federal income tax (Income Tax Act s. 96); the LP is fiscally transparent and profits are allocated to and taxed at the partner level; a non-resident limited partner is taxable on Canadian-source business income only to the extent the partnership carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada or Quebec (ITA s. 253; Quebec Taxation Act s. 22); for GST/HST and QST purposes the partnership is treated as a separate registrant person; no territorial or tax-exempt-zone treatment applies to ordinary Quebec wholesale alcohol activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the governing partnership law. Available federal and Quebec elections include: (i) combined GST/HST and QST registration and joint remittance election with Revenu Quebec; (ii) optional GST/HST registration for a small supplier (ETA s. 240(2.1)); (iii) ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations (not relevant to this LP); (iv) partnership fiscal-period and capital-cost allowance elections affecting the computation of partner income; (v) Quebec QST group election for qualifying corporations; (vi) hybrid-mismatch and anti-deferral rules under ITA ss. 18.4 to 18.6, which operate mechanically rather than electively, so no neutrality election is available to shield cross-border deductible payments from recharacterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT regime: federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST, Excise Tax Act Part IX) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST, Loi sur la taxe de vente du Quebec, RLRQ c T-0.1), administered jointly by CRA and Revenu Quebec; beer excise duty under the Excise Act, 2001 and SAQ permitting under the Quebec Alcoholic Beverages Act apply in parallel but are not VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - small-supplier threshold measured over the current calendar quarter and the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters for both GST/HST and QST; a non-resident LP making taxable beer supplies in Canada or Quebec must register once the threshold is exceeded; the wholesale revenue volume of this craft beer distribution LP will exceed CAD 30,000 in the first operating quarter, making compulsory registration immediate; voluntary registration remains available below the threshold (ETA s. 240).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API tax pre-clearance, or digital stamping for B2B beer wholesale invoices. CRA and Revenu Quebec accept EDI and Peppol-based Pan-Canadian e-invoicing on a voluntary basis; exporters must report shipments through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), with G13-equivalent declarations and PARS/ACI e-manifest data for transported goods; Quebec SAQ packaging and distribution rules impose machine-readable labels and excise stamps, but these are not fiscal e-invoicing stamps.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Beer supplied to a foreign recipient qualifies for zero-rating where possession passes in Canada and the goods are exported as soon as is reasonably possible after delivery (ETA Sch. VI Part V; QST mirror rules in QSTA ss. 26 to 28.0.1). The LP must retain documentary evidence that the export occurred (shipment from Canada to a foreign destination and foreign customs clearance) and that the supply was made for use outside Canada; ancillary cold-chain freight and insurance services supplied to the non-resident buyer are also zero-rated where they form part of the exported supply; sales to US and other NAFTA/foreign buyers are zero-rated rather than exempt; a qualifying export permits the LP to claim input tax credits and Quebec input tax refunds in the same return cycle.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or G13, or an outward foreign cargo manifest evidencing actual exportation from Canada
Original or electronic Bill of Lading, air waybill or CMR issued to the LP showing a foreign destination and a consignee outside Canada
Commercial invoice, packing list, keg-return evidence, certificate of analysis, and Excise Act, 2001 removal documentation for the alcoholic beverage
Inward Remittance Certificate: SWIFT MT103, bank FX conversion voucher, or equivalent proof that the export sale proceeds were repatriated to the LP's Canadian bank account on time
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reverse the zero-rating on reassessment where the documentary bundle is incomplete, restoring GST/HST and QST at 14.975% on the invoice value plus arrears interest and penalties; the false statement penalty is 25% of the net tax (50% for wilful misstatement) under ETA s. 285.1 and equivalent QST penalty provisions; tax evasion carries criminal fines up to 200% of the tax at risk and imprisonment under ETA s. 327.1; the 180-day repatriation covenant is a programmatic compliance condition consistent with CRA administrative expectations for export proceeds, and failure to repatriate within the deadline may trigger income inclusion for the non-resident partners, Part XIII withholding exposure, denial or clawback of input tax credits on the exported kegs, and retrospective recovery of previously credited refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); there is no separate Foreign Exchange Administration, as Canada operates under a market-determined exchange rate regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account items. Profit distributions, capital repatriation, repayment of shareholder loans, and partnership redemptions are freely permitted without exchange control authorization. Non-resident limited partners receive CAD or foreign currency remittances without Canadian Foreign Exchange Act approval, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax and reporting obligations under the Income Tax Act, Canada Revenue Agency notification requirements, and FINTRAC large cross-border wire transaction reporting thresholds. The Canadian Dollar is a free-floating currency with no surrender or conversion quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed timeline for export proceeds in Canada. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency, deposited to a foreign-currency bank account licensed under the Bank Act, or converted at commercial rates at the exporter's discretion. Records of export invoices, proof of receipt, and underlying sales contracts must be retained for Income Tax Act and Excise Act purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary payment services provider, Low as a primary settlement bank. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not Canadian chartered banks and cannot lawfully hold Canadian client deposits for business treasury settlement under the Bank Act. A Quebec Limited Partnership may use an authorized FX payment platform for cross-border payment execution, but the primary account must sit with a Canadian regulated deposit-taking institution or a registered foreign bank branch. Legal constraints include unauthorized deposit-taking exposure, FINTRAC MSB registration obligations if the platform handles Canadian funds, and uncertainty in Canadian insolvency law regarding funds held by unregulated EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is widely permitted by Tier 1 Canadian banks using electronic identity verification, corporate document validation, and live video confirmation. Physical attendance is not absolutely mandated; however, banks retain discretion to require an in-branch interview of the general partner's authorized signatories and all 25%+ beneficial owners where beneficial-ownership layers, non-resident partners, or PEP involvement generate enhanced due diligence triggers. For Quebec limited partnerships, the corporate general partner's directors are normally the relevant control individuals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registraire des entreprises extract showing the LP declaration and general partner, full partnership agreement, an organizational chart tracing all partners through each intermediary, personal identification for every ultimate beneficial owner, and statutory declaration confirming no undisclosed beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner in a high-risk jurisdiction or with significant foreign funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth report supported by bank references, audited financial statements of the foreign investing entity, tax residency certificates, OECD CRS self-certification forms, partnership capital account statements, and notarized confirmations that funds derive from lawful commercial activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alcohol distribution licence and regulatory consistency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of the Québec liquor permit issued under the Société des alcools du Québec (SAQ) framework, Registraire des entreprises business licence, municipal permits, craft brewery supply agreements, and evidence of provincial excise duty registration where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas trade payments involving third-party intermediaries and freight forwarders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply, warehousing, and logistics contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs entry forms, freight forwarder credentials, and a documented three-way matching trail among purchase orders, invoices, and receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital contributions or high-velocity cross-border wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership capital call notices, subscription agreements, source-of-funds letters from remitting banks, board resolutions of the general partner, and a treasury protocol demonstrating FINTRAC cross-border wire report filing readiness for transactions at CAD 10,000 or above.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US dollar settlement activity triggering US Correspondent Banking concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Downstream customer KYC files for wholesale distributors, beneficial-ownership certificates for corporate clients, end-user attestations for beer purchases, and anti-money laundering compliance policies under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound non-resident equity and partner loan capital must be routed by SWIFT MT103 to the Quebec LP's Canadian-dollar or US-dollar bank account using the bank's standard transit number, institution number, and SWIFT/BIC. Payment references must state 'Capital Contribution to CA LP' or 'Partner Loan Advance', and the remittance must include the LP's legal name and Quebec enterprise registration number. The bank will verify the ultimate originator under FINTRAC client identification rules; any international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC. For inbound funds exceeding CAD 50,000, the bank may require a capital call notice, signed partnership agreement extract, and confirmation from the receiving partner that funds are not sourced from unlawful activity. Use of shell intermediary accounts is prohibited; pre-funding treasury verification is required to match the remitter with an identified limited partner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported hops, malt, kegs, packaging, and equipment will clear via SWIFT MT103 for international supplier payments, with payment terms referenced in the 70-field remittance information. For documentary trade, Commercial Letters of Credit are issued through a Canadian chartered bank using SWIFT MT700/MT707, typically at sight or with a 60-day tenor; required documents include commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and certificate of origin. Domestically, Canadian-dollar supplier payments are cleared through Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for high-priority wires; US-dollar domestic payment concentration may be handled via the bank's US clearing network and ACH rails when appropriate. Standby LCs may support performance and trade deposits with US counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards involving CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP with Tier 1 Canadian banks under negotiated ISDA and CSA agreements
FX swaps and rollover forward contracts for managing short-term cash-flow mismatches
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-fixed or floating-for-fixed) used to synthetically convert foreign-currency debt into Canadian-dollar liabilities
Over-the-counter FX options (puts and calls) covered by eligible derivatives dealer arrangements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible for hedges on currencies without deliverable CAD markets, but CAD itself is fully deliverable and therefore NDF contracts on CAD are not recommended and rarely offered by Canadian banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration to the Registraire des entreprises / Déclaration annuelle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of initial registration; thereafter annually no later than the registration anniversary date selected by the partnership; filing is available online through the Registraire portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative penalty and interest; failure to file for three consecutive fiscal periods can result in administrative cancellation/strike-off of the limited partnership registration and loss of legal publicity protections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return and T5013 supplementary slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for other fiscal year-ends, due within 90 days after the partnership fiscal period end; no extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA may assess late-filing penalties under the Income Tax Act, charge daily penalties for unreported partner allocations, and require amended T5013 slips; continued non-filing can trigger an administrative audit and penal interest accumulation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of Alcohol Wholesaler Permit / Permis de grossiste d'alcool
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Régie des alcools, des jeux et des courses / Société des alcools du Québec licensing directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal must be filed and paid before the permit anniversary date shown on the existing permit; the regulator normally issues a renewal notice 60 days before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An expired permit is void; the partnership must immediately cease distribution activities. Operating without a valid permit constitutes a penal offence with fines per day on legal entities, potential seizure of alcoholic inventory, and suspension of permit eligibility for repeat non-renewal.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Quebec or federal statute imposes a compulsory external audit on this limited partnership solely by reason of entity type, size, or revenues. Mandatory independent certified audit arises only where (i) the partnership agreement or an agreement of limited partners requires it; (ii) a lender, surety, or institutional investor imposes an audit covenant; (iii) the alcohol permit regulator conditions continued licensing on audited financial statements; or (iv) a court, CRA, or Revenu Québec orders a statutory audit or financial review after default, inspection, or investment-security filings. In all other cases the partnership may rely on internal compiled financial information.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook Part II – Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); IFRS (Part I) is required only if the partnership has public accountability, is a reporting issuer, or is voluntarily designated as an IFRS reporter. ASPE is the customary framework for a Quebec limited partnership engaged in craft beer distribution.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner shall perform an annual UBO confirmation review immediately before filing the annual declaration. Each limited partner must confirm on record the identity of every individual with significant control, the nature of control, and whether any transfer of partnership interests occurred during the reporting year. Any change in persons with significant control, including transfers of limited partnership interests exceeding the thresholds in Quebec legal publicity obligations, must be recorded internally within 30 days of becoming known and reflected in the annual declaration update filed with the Registraire des entreprises.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book / Resolutions and Consent Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 240 – 700 (typical Quebec registered office or registered agent service in the greater Montreal area)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,700 – 10,400 (certified audit for a craft beer distribution LP; compilation or review engaged at USD 1,100 – 2,600 where no statutory audit applies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the LP level (flow-through entity); allocated income is taxed in the partners' hands — combined general corporate rate for a corporate partner in Quebec: 15% federal + 11.5% Quebec = 26.5%; qualifying CCPC active business income: 9% + 3.2% = 12.2%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a CCPC); Quebec small-business rate reduction (Quebec Tax Act s. 771.1: rate reduced to 3.2%); SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPCs on qualified expenditures, 15% general); no entity-level tax on the LP itself; partner-level graduated rates for Canadian individual partners (same as personal tax brackets).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 – Summary of Partnership Income (with T5013 slips, Schedule 50); electronically transmitted via CRA EFILE/Internet File Transfer through approved third-party software or through a registered professional filer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end (e.g., May 31 where the fiscal period ends on December 31).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total partnership income (loss) from active cold-chain wholesale beer distribution, before allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners: report only the Canadian-source portion of that business income; the amount is treated as Canadian-source business income of the partner, attracting Part I filing obligations and, where applicable, Part XIII withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from investments conducted outside the active distribution business (e.g., interest on corporate deposits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partner, investment-type income may be a passive Part XIII source (25% statutory) rather than Part I active business income; review treaty character rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocable share of business income, taxable capital gains, charitable donations and tax credits attributed to each partner in accordance with the LP agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner's allocable share is calculated using the LP agreement's economic-sharing ratio; the LP must collect the partner's name, residence and TRC (if available).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013 return: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500). Per unpaid/misfiled T5013 slip: CAD 50 per slip per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per slip), plus arrears interest on any unreported partner tax. A false statement can attract the s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of the federally evaded amount.
